topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text: I come home from the fields, back ache and hands sore, to find my wife in a daze, her face pale as the winter moon. She stammers, hands fidgeting, and admits to writing a book. A book, mind you, not just any words on parchment, but a tale spun from our life, our sweat, our toil. I toil in the soil, dawn to dusk, while she scribes our struggles and spills them to the world. What good is this fancy writing? It’s our life, our privy thoughts and pains, laid bare. If the neighbors find out, if they laugh or pity, where will my dignity stand? This soil is harsh, but it keeps its secrets, unlike ink on a page.
